title: Standardized patient: abdominal pain
intro: Door card: Mr. Tyler Brooks, 22, "stomach pain". Twelve minutes, history and a focused abdominal exam.

steps.say: Mr. Brooks lies very still on his side, knees drawn up. He winces when you close the door.

options.text: Introduce yourself, acknowledge that he's in pain, and tell him you'll be quick and gentle.
options.reply: "Thanks. It really hurts." He manages a smile.

options.text: Ask him to sit up and walk to the exam table so it's easier to examine him.
options.reply: He tries, then stops, holding his side. Every movement hurts: that's a clue in itself.
He answers in short, tight sentences.

choice.lesson: Acknowledge pain and explain what you'll do before you start

history.opening: "It started in the middle last night. Now it's all down here." He points to his right lower abdomen.

items.ask: Where did it start, and where is it now?
items.answer: "Around my belly button. This morning it moved down here, on the right."

items.ask: Does moving or coughing make it worse?
items.answer: "The car ride over was agony: every bump."

items.ask: Have you felt sick or vomited? How's your appetite?
items.answer: "I threw up twice. I don't want to eat anything."
"I felt hot and shivery this morning."

items.ask: Any burning when you pee, or blood in your urine?
Any pain or swelling in your testicles?
Have you had anything like this before? Any medical problems or allergies?
When did you last eat or drink?
items.answer: "A sandwich yesterday lunchtime. Sips of water since."

maneuvers.name: Palpate at McBurney's point
maneuvers.finding: Marked tenderness a third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus, with guarding.

maneuvers.name: Press on the left lower quadrant
maneuvers.finding: Pressing on the left causes pain on the right: Rovsing sign is positive.

maneuvers.name: Check for peritonism
maneuvers.finding: Gentle percussion over the right lower quadrant makes him flinch; he won't cough without holding his side.

maneuvers.name: Extend the right hip
maneuvers.finding: Pain on extending the hip: the psoas sign is positive.

maneuvers.name: Check the kidney angles
maneuvers.finding: No tenderness at the costovertebral angles.

choice.prompt: "Am I going to need an operation?"

options.text: "It may well be your appendix. The surgeons will see you and explain everything, and it's often a keyhole operation. I'll make sure they know how much pain you're in."
options.reply: He nods, relieved to have a straight answer.
He goes pale. It isn't your decision to make, and he'll hold you to it.
He looks away. He's frightened and alone with it.

choice.lesson: Be honest about what you think, within your role, and say who will decide

feedback: "Textbook. You examined the abdomen as gently as you took the history."
"Good. Always ask when they last ate: the anesthetist will."
"Review appendicitis: migration, anorexia, fever, McBurney's point, Rovsing. Then practice on a classmate."
